source_snapshot.procedure:
【Before Test】
    1. Check that the SUT configuration (e.g., hardware, firmware, drivers, etc.) matches the specifications/recipe definition.
    2. Clear logs (e.g., dmesg, syslog, SEL, etc.).

    【During Test】
    1. Power on system and boot to USB Key.
2. Install Windows Server OS (with GUI)
3. Check OS event logs.

    【After Test】
    1. Collect test results and photos, and save them to specific folders.
    2. Check if there are unexpected logs (e.g., dmesg, syslog, SEL, etc.) generate after test.
source_snapshot.criteria:
1. Os Installation should be completed successfully
2. System should be workable after reboot
3. System event log should not have error/fail/warning messages (except the message is a known event.

deepseek_columns.ai_commands: Agent assists a directed non-interactive/scripted Windows installation after RAID VD setup.
deepseek_columns.ai_logs_output: OS boot, RAID VD visibility and layout verification.
deepseek_columns.risk: OS install partitions/formats the RAID volume; use only the user-designated VD.

historical_reviews.deepseek: PARTIAL; recognizes installer media and destructive RAID-volume targeting but leaves identity and evidence underspecified.
historical_reviews.gpt_v2: REQUIRES PACKAGE / USER CONFIRMATION / IMPROVED; adds exact RAID VD, image, driver, UEFI mode, backup, OOB recovery and known-event allowlist.

original_test_intent: Install the approved Windows Server GUI image from USB media onto the designated RAID virtual disk, prove the system remains usable after reboot, and evaluate Windows event logs against an approved known-event list.
original_method: A qualified operator connects and selects the approved USB installer and confirms the RAID virtual-disk target; an unattended answer file or controlled installer performs partitioning and installation, then post-reboot automation verifies boot, storage layout, controller health and exported Windows events.
manual_activity: The source explicitly requires boot from a USB key. A person must attach/identify the approved medium and confirm the destructive RAID VD at the installer boundary; after this physical setup and confirmation, unattended installation and evidence collection can automate the core deployment checks.
required_inputs: Windows Server edition/build/language image, checksum and license policy
Exact RAID controller and virtual-disk identity, size, boot role and serial/member mapping
Signed RAID driver and injection/loading method
USB media/operator or approved equivalent project override
Known-event allowlist with provider, event ID and time window
Backup/reimage plan, OOB credentials and maintenance window
safety_requirements: Never select a disk by order alone; bind the target to controller VD identity and approved capacity/members.
Do not partition or format an OS, mounted, in-use, protected, data-bearing or unknown VD outside the approved plan.
Capture rather than clear baseline Windows/controller/BMC logs; preserve installer failures.
Do not automatically retry installation, repartition, change boot order or reimage after failure.
Stop on target/image/driver mismatch, inaccessible OOB recovery, controller degradation or unexpected storage inventory.
agent_execution_scope: Verify media hash, target identity, driver set, answer file and recovery gates before installation.
Run the unchanged approved unattended install after operator media/target confirmation and monitor explicit setup phases.
After reboot, collect Windows build, boot/storage mapping, controller state and filtered/full event exports.
Compare actual evidence with expected values and report Tool Result without setting PASS/FAIL.
engineer_actions: Provide/attach the approved USB key and confirm boot selection and exact RAID VD.
Approve destructive install scope and recovery plan.
Approve the known-event allowlist and decide the formal verdict.

command_applicability.original_deepseek_command_fit: Conceptually aligned but not executable: it provides no installer answer file, media identity, VD binding, RAID driver or evidence commands.
command_applicability.command_recommendation: Retain USB boot and Windows Server GUI coverage; use a reviewed unattend.xml and controller-specific driver only if the project approves them, with post-install PowerShell event export and storage identity checks.
command_applicability.original_parameters_and_time_preserved: USB-key boot, Windows Server GUI, event-log review and 10/20-minute source fields are retained; actual install time is platform dependent.

modernized_recommendation.recommended_method: Use checksum-verified media and answer file bound to the approved RAID VD, retain setup logs, then export System/Application events and reconcile the boot volume to the RAID controller after restart.
modernized_recommendation.applicable_platform: Exact Windows Server build, RAID adapter/driver, firmware and boot mode.
modernized_recommendation.supported_version: Record image/build, unattend revision, RAID driver, controller firmware and BIOS/BMC versions.
modernized_recommendation.official_reference: Microsoft Windows Setup/unattended installation documentation and controller vendor driver/installation guide.
modernized_recommendation.difference_from_original_method: Automates repeatable installer inputs and evidence after the required media/target confirmation.
modernized_recommendation.coverage_difference: No reduction; GUI image and USB boot remain represented.
modernized_recommendation.required_inputs: Image, target, driver, layout and event allowlist.
modernized_recommendation.risks_limitations: An unattended file can rapidly destroy the wrong VD if identity binding is weak.

project_override_considerations: The engineer may approve virtual media/PXE instead of a physical USB key, but the record must identify that override and may claim only the approved image, VD and deployment path—not the untouched original USB path.
expected_evidence: Media/image hash, answer-file revision, exact controller/VD/drive mapping and approval
Installer logs, selected target, partition result, driver load and setup completion status
Post-reboot Windows build, boot volume, RAID health and workable-system checks
Full event exports plus allowlist comparison, BMC/SEL window, Tool Result and engineer verdict

source_conflict_analysis.analysis: Procedure and criteria consistently cover installation, reboot usability and event health. Missing image, target and known-event definitions are project inputs rather than contradictory source facts.

blocked_analysis.analysis: The test intent is executable once the project supplies media, target, driver, allowlist and recovery controls; those omissions do not justify permanent BLOCKED.

comparison_to_prior_reviews.deepseek: Keeps the hybrid conclusion while replacing its vague target statement with stable VD identity and complete installation evidence.
comparison_to_prior_reviews.gpt_v2: Agrees with its safety model and makes the physical USB setup the precise reason for the V3.1 partial class.
comparison_to_prior_reviews.v3_1_improvement: Separates setup media/approval, automated execution status, Tool Result and engineer verdict.

review_improvement: Makes the destructive boundary enforceable and the event-log exception auditable without misclassifying missing media as BLOCKED.
independent_technical_reasoning: Windows deployment and validation can be automated, but the stated USB-medium setup and high-consequence target confirmation require a human boundary. That fits the locked partial class, not MANUAL ONLY, because the installation and evidence path can then run automatically.
no_automatic_retry: Do not restart setup, repartition, change boot order or reimage automatically. Preserve the failed phase and obtain engineer direction.
